newsitem.title: MEXICO: France's GFA to build electricity plant in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: France's GFA to build electricity plant in Mexico.

text.p: French construction firm GFA said on Wednesday it plans to start work next year on an electric power plant near this western Mexican city, investing at least $1.3 billion over the next four years.

"The work will begin in a years' time, and it should be four years from now before the plant actually gets underway," company president Grancois Abballe told a news conference. He said the total investment would be between $1.3 billion and $1.5 billion.
The plant will run on natural gas and generate up to 1,150 megawatts of electricity, which will supply nearby companies.
GFA officials said 45 companies in the area have already signed agreements to buy energy from the plant.
Abballe said the company will provide 30 percent of the project's financing, with the remaining money coming from Mexican and international banks.

He said the company would sell energy at a cheaper rate than that provided by Mexico's state-run Federal Electricity Commission. Mexico in recent years has begun allowing private generation of electricity, previously the exclusive domain of the government.
